body.statement:
At every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), meaning that every bounded factorwise centered additive latent score generates for all sufficiently small positive and negative path parameters a product-factor path remaining in \(\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the full observed-data tangent space satisfies \(\mathcal T=\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}^{\,L^2(P)}\).  At such a \(P\),
\[
\mathcal T^{\perp}=\{k\in L^2_0(P):E(k\mid Y,J,X)=E(k\mid A,J,X)=E(k\mid Z,J,X)=0\}.
\]
body.justification: Equality with the full observed DQM closure, not merely a convenient submodel score span, is the key efficiency theorem.
body.gap: Continuous full-law recovery in Hu and Schennach and its triple-proxy causal use in Deaner are identification statements, not a measurable uniformly bounded inverse of the derivative of the factor map. The binary tangent calculation in Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen also does not establish that multilevel DQM lifting on the stated regular stratum.
body.consumer: It turns the candidate variance calculation into the information bound for every regular estimator of the smoking-level contrasts.
body.proof_tex:
The affirmative differential-inverse resolution places every observed DQM score in \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\).  Taking closures gives
\[
\mathcal T\subseteq\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}^{\,L^2(P)}. \tag{24}
\]
Conversely, at the stated two-sided pathwise-interior point, every bounded factorwise centered additive score generates an admissible product-factor DQM path.  Differentiating its product likelihood shows that its observed score is its conditional expectation given \(O\), and hence belongs to \(\mathcal T\).  Truncation followed by factorwise recentering makes bounded scores dense in each factor \(L^2\) space; conditional expectation is an \(L^2\) contraction.  Since \(\mathcal T\) is closed, this proves the reverse inclusion in (24), and therefore equality.

For the orthocomplement, take \(k\in L^2_0(P)\).  Conditional-expectation duality says that orthogonality to every centered outcome-factor score is equivalent to
\[
E(k\mid Y,J,X)=E(k\mid J,X). \tag{25}
\]
The analogous statements with \(A\) and \(Z\) replace \(Y\) in (25).  Orthogonality to centered propensity scores is equivalent to \(E(k\mid J,X)=E(k\mid X)\), and orthogonality to marginal \(X\)-scores is equivalent to \(E(k\mid X)=E(k)=0\).  Thus orthogonality to the additive score image implies all three conditional expectations in the theorem are zero.

Conversely, if the three displayed conditional expectations are zero, the first already implies \(E(k\mid J,X)=E(k\mid X)=0\), and each factorwise inner product vanishes by iterated expectation.  Hence \(k\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and therefore to its closure \(\mathcal T\).  This proves the asserted characterization.
